data.label: Project built by shah Date: 2026-8-19 --The Problem   Client websites (US Auto Connection, Rickenbaugh) were losing their widgets with 404 errors after deployments, forcing   clients to repeatedly re-paste embed code.   Root Cause   . scripts/build-widget.mjs published the shared widget bundle under a content-hashed filename (widget.<hash>.js) on ev     y build, and the dashboard's "Copy Code" modal embedded that hashed URL into client snippets via /widget-manifest.js     .   . The hashed files were gitignored, so each Vercel deploy contained only that build's hash - any redeploy made every p     viously embedded snippet 404, killing all widgets on client sites.   The Fix (3 files changed)   1. src/components/WidgetsHome.tsx - Embed snippets now always use the permanent URL /api/embeds/widget.js; removed the      nifest fetch and hashed-path logic.   2. next.config.ts - Added a rewrite: any request for a legacy widget.<16-hex>.js file that no longer exists is forward      to /api/embeds/widget.js, retroactively healing all broken embeds already on client sites. Removed the obsolete imm      ble-cache header rules.   3. scripts/build-widget.mjs - Stopped generating hashed copies and widget-manifest.json; cleaned up 35 stale hashed fi      from local public/.   Verification   . ? npm run build:widget passes, tsc --noEmit passes, eslint passes   . ? Live-tested both broken hashes from the chat (ae8df6f21595663e, cb1d7a5b739d2865) - they now return 200 with the     ll bundle instead of 404   Result: embed codes are now paste-once, works-forever. Old snippets heal automatically after deploy; new snippets neve   r break.   Architecture Explanation (per your questions)   . The snippet has 2 scripts: data.js (URL contains the widget ID ? server queries Supabase ? returns pure data: kind,     nfig, business, reviews) and widget.js (the shared engine - identical for everyone).   . Rendering is 100% client-side: widget.js (a minified Preact app with all widget components + bundled CSS) scans the     ge for data-bbs-embed divs, reads the ID, pulls that ID's payload from window.__BBS_WIDGET_DATA__, picks the right c     ponent by kind, and builds the DOM inside a Shadow DOM bubble.   . Styling: base CSS is bundled into the engine and injected into the shadow root; per-widget styling (colors, font, la     ut) comes from the config in data.js and is applied as inline styles - which is why dashboard edits propagate to all     lient sites automatically with no re-embedding.---  1. Created the Form widget editor page - src/app/widgets/form/page.tsx: lists form_widgets from Supabase, maps each to a FormEditorWidget, and pre-selects the ?id= widget (mirrors the before-after page pattern).  2. Registered Multi-Step Form in the dashboard (src/components/WidgetsHome.tsx):  New type card with emerald icon + FormMock preview (Grid ? click ? modal) createForm (POSTs defaults, navigates to editor) and duplicateForm Delete routed through /api/v1/form-widgets/:id; modal grid shows live FormWidget preview with edit/copy-code/duplicate/delete Wired into WidgetTypeKey, widgetTypeMeta, list state, search, and Create New button 3. Verified the embed path - data.js, the widget.js bundle loader, registry, and prefetch already handled the form kind, so copy-code works unchanged.  4. Fixed pre-existing type errors in the form feature: form-tabs.tsx (invalid visibilityRule!['operator'] cast ? VisibilityOperator), form-config.ts (added required? to FormFieldValidation), FormWidget.tsx (textAlign cast).  5. Verification - tsc --noEmit clean, eslint 0 errors, npm run build:widget (84kb minified), unit tests 20 passed.  6. Applied the Supabase migration - 017_form_widgets.sql existed but was never run; applied it via npm run migrate. Verified form_widgets + form_submissions tables now exist and the demo form (f3612ca6-.) is seeded. (Before this, the whole feature would 500 at runtime.)  7. Defaults request (in progress) - you want specific fields/steps as the default for new forms. I can't read your screenshots/files (model has no vision support) - awaiting your text description of the exact fields/steps and order.  Note: my one-shot build:widget check minified public/widget.js (the dev watch:widget build is unminified) - no code was lost.
